structured.answer: I'd go with option ג, the one that's like א but also shows past returns and how big each fund is. In there I'd take the S&P 500 track at Menora (מנורה מבטחים): it's at the top, has the lowest fee of the 12 (0.52%) and about 13.8% over 3 years.

stuck.why: The list just keeps going: S&P, then מניות, then עוקב מדדי מניות. A dozen near-identical rows per group with the same company names and fees between 0.52% and 0.73%. I lost track of which group I was in.
Each row has two fees, 'מהחיסכון' and 'מההפקדות'. I don't know which one is the real fee I'd pay, so I just looked at the first one.

stuck.where: The top of section ג, screen 7
stuck.why: It looked like the same table starting a third time. I nearly stopped there before I saw the returns column.

findings.what: In א and ב there's no past return at all, so I can't tell which one does better. Only ג has it, and that's what made me pick it.
The page is endlessly long: the same table three times, with dozens of rows that look alike. On a phone I'd give up in the middle.
Two fees in every row with no explanation of which one counts. And the percentages (0.52% vs 0.71%) look like nothing to me. I'd want to see it in shekels.
The מט"ח column and the rings aren't explained next to them. I don't understand why one S&P has 97% and a 'stocks' fund has 26%.
There's no 'what to do now' button. The arrow at the end of the row doesn't say where it goes.
In ג some funds show 'פחות מ־3 שנים' instead of a return, so they look like they have nothing to show.
